rivalry.rationale: India fragrances (~US$2.6bn perfume+deodorant, LOW) is led in mass by Vini Cosmetics/Fogg (FY25 revenue INR 1,200cr, KKR-controlled) with many domestic deo/perfume players, while a wave of D2C fragrance entrants is drawing investor money. A dominant mass player plus an active D2C challenger field indicates high intensity.
evidence: fragrances.json IN size US$2.6bn (perfume+deo, LOW); Vini Cosmetics/Fogg FY25 rev INR1200cr (MEDIUM, NET_REALISATION)
india_findings.yaml new_players: KKR owns 54% of Vini Cosmetics/Fogg (US$1.2bn valuation)
fragrances.json IN revenue point source: 'investors catch a big whiff of money in D2C fragrance firms' (ET)

buyer_power.rationale: Premium/perfume distribution runs through beauty platforms taking Nykaa fragrance commission of 22-25%, while mass deodorant flows through fragmented GT/MT. Channel leverage is meaningful at the premium end but diluted across mass retail.
evidence: colour_cosmetics.json IN trade_margin note: same Nykaa guide states fragrances 22-25% commission
fragrances.json IN import_dependence note: mass perfume/deodorant domestically filled

supplier_power.rationale: Premium fragrance is import-reliant — UAE is India's largest perfume-import source (HS 3303), then France/Germany for high-end oils — so premium entrants depend on overseas suppliers of oils and finished juice, raising input-side leverage. Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled, so the higher supplier power is scoped to the premium tier.
evidence: india_findings.yaml import_make: premium fragrance import-reliant, UAE largest source then France/Germany; mass domestically filled
fragrances.json IN import_value HS3303 US$0.332bn from world (2024, HIGH); import_dependence 12.8% (ESTIMATE)

new_entrant_threat.rationale: Mass perfume/deodorant is domestically filled via contract manufacturing and D2C fragrance is actively funded, so domestic launch is cheap and well-capitalised. Premium entrants instead face import friction (CDSCO COS-1 to COS-2 plus overseas oil sourcing), so the threat is high for domestic-fill entrants and moderated for import-led premium.
evidence: fragrances.json IN revenue source: strong D2C fragrance funding ('big whiff of money', ET)
india_findings.yaml supply_chain: contract-manufacturing base; import_make: premium import-reliant + CDSCO
corridor.yaml regulation: CDSCO COS-1 to COS-2 via SUGAM (import friction)

substitutes.rationale: The segment itself bundles fine perfume with deodorant/body-mist, and the dominant volume sits in cheaper deo/mist formats — evidencing substitution between premium perfume and mass deodorant within the same demand space. Substitution is directional given the combined-basket sizing.
evidence: fragrances.json IN size note: US$2.6bn is 'perfume+DEODORANT combined', broader than perfume-only US$0.281bn
fragrances.json IN import_dependence note: mass perfume/deodorant domestically filled (the cheaper substitute layer)

overall.rationale: India fragrances is a growing, mass-led market with a dominant deo incumbent (Fogg) and easy domestic entry, but the premium tier an import-led K-beauty entrant would target is supplier-dependent (UAE/France) and channel-gated. Attractive on demand, but premium entry carries import and supplier friction; the KR-IN corridor flow itself is negligible.
evidence: fragrances.json IN size US$2.6bn + premium import-reliance; KR-IN corridor imports US$0.000135bn (2024)
